**Section C: Comprehension**

*Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions below it. In answering use complete and correct English sentences and, as much as possible, your own words.*

**A waste of space**

It has been seen as a stepping stone on the way to Mars, an example of international co-operation in space, and an orbiting research laboratory. Sadly, the international space station is none of these things. Sixteen years after Ronald Reagan set NASA, America's space agency, the goal of establishing a permanently manned orbital outpost, its first residents are due to blast off on October 31st and get on board their new home on November 2nd, mission controllers will no doubt cheer, champagne corks will pop and there will be much talk of mankind taking bold steps into space. But the truth is that the space station, which will take until at least 2006 to complete, at a cost of over US\$100 billion, is a monumental waste of time and money.

Its original purpose, 5onceived in the cold-war spirit of 1984, vas to assert Arnerica's might as a space-faring superpower. That version of the station, dubbed FREEDOM, was due to be completed by 1994, at a cost of US\$8 billion. But Mr Reagan's successor, Georges Bush, unveiled a change of plan in 1989, on the 2Oth anniversary of the Apollo moon landing. The station, he announced, would now be completed by 1999, in preparation for the launching of a manned mission to Mars in 2019.

This objective was, in tum, quickly put aside. NASA worked out how much a Mars mission would cost: a staggering US$ 450 billion. Instead, the European, Canadian and Japanese space agencies agreed to get involved with the station, which was positioned once again - this time as a model for international co-operation in space. And in 1993, with the cold war over, the Russians were invited to join in too. The space involvement of the Russians reduced the chances of that country's rocket scientists going off to work for Iran or north Korea, and was also expected to save US$ 2 billion through cheaper technology and reduced launch cost.

In the event, Russian involvement has proved a disaster. It has cost America, the dominant member of the 16-nation consortium that is now building the station, an additional US\$3 billion in delays and hand-out to the cash - strapped Russian space programme. Russian components of the station do not come up to American safety standards, and will require expensive "on-orbit" modifications. Worst of all, Russia has still not got rid of its ancient MIR Space station, thus raising suspicions about its commitment to the international project nor does the station have much scientific merit. Indeed, few scientists - other than those whose livelihood depend on it - have a kind word to say about the enterprise, since robots would be able to do pretty well all of the experiment proposed for less money and less risk to human life. But perhaps the greatest irony is that since Georges Bush's rash promise to send people to Mars, the cost of doing so has dropped dramatically. The price of a manned landing, based on a radical new mission plan that involves extracting fuel for the return trip from the martian atmosphere, is currently put at around US\$30 billion - less than a third of the cost of the space station. Instead of wasting years of effort and billions of dollars constructing a pointless castle in the sky, NASA could have followed both its scientific and populist instincts, and gone to Mars anyway.

*From The Economist, October 28th 2000*

**Questions:**

Le texte donne trois indices convergents qui justifient le jugement de l'auteur : le coût faramineux de la station (plus de 100 milliards de dollars), le retard considérable pris sur le calendrier initial (achèvement repoussé à 2006 au moins), et surtout l'absence d'utilité scientifique réelle du projet, puisque des robots pourraient réaliser la quasi-totalité des expériences prévues pour moins cher et avec moins de risques pour la vie humaine.

**Réponse rédigée (en anglais) :**
"The construction of the space station is a monumental waste of time and money because it will take until at least 2006 to complete, at a cost of over US\$100 billion, while robots could carry out nearly all the planned experiments more cheaply and with less risk to human life than astronauts."

### Rappel de méthode

Pour une question Vrai/Faux, la justification doit citer ou paraphraser la phrase exacte du texte qui confirme ou infirme l'affirmation.

### Corrigé
(Le texte source contient plusieurs coquilles de saisie déjà présentes dans le sujet original : "5onceived" pour "conceived", "vas" pour "was", "Arnerica's" pour "America's", "2Oth" pour "20th", "tum" pour "turn". Elles sont reproduites telles quelles dans l'énoncé par souci de fidélité au document, et neutralisées dans la lecture du corrigé ci-dessous.)

Il faut relever deux dates dans le texte. La version originale du projet, baptisée FREEDOM, "was due to be completed by 1994" (devait être achevée en 1994). Or, le tout premier paragraphe précise que la station actuelle "will take until at least 2006 to complete" (ne sera pas achevée avant 2006 au plus tôt). L'écart entre la date prévue à l'origine (1994) et la date réelle d'achèvement (2006 au minimum) est donc de 2006 - 1994 = 12 ans.

Réponse : **(b) For 12 years**

questions.enonce_markdown: 5. The Russian involvement with the station met American’s expectation. True or False? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un QCM ou une question Vrai/Faux de compréhension se résout en revenant systématiquement au passage du texte qui permet de trancher, jamais par impression générale. Pour une question Vrai/Faux, la justification doit citer ou paraphraser la phrase exacte du texte qui confirme ou infirme l'affirmation.

### Corrigé
(Le texte source contient plusieurs coquilles de saisie déjà présentes dans le sujet original : "5onceived" pour "conceived", "vas" pour "was", "Arnerica's" pour "America's", "2Oth" pour "20th", "tum" pour "turn". Elles sont reproduites telles quelles dans l'énoncé par souci de fidélité au document, et neutralisées dans la lecture du corrigé ci-dessous.)

Le texte est sans ambiguïté : "In the event, Russian involvement has proved a disaster." Au lieu de l'économie de 2 milliards de dollars espérée, l'implication russe a coûté 3 milliards de dollars supplémentaires aux États-Unis en retards et en aides financières, et les composants russes ne respectent même pas les normes de sécurité américaines. L'affirmation est donc fausse.

Réponse : **False**

**Justification rédigée (en anglais) :**
"False. Russian involvement did not meet America's expectations: instead of saving money, it has cost America an additional US\$3 billion in delays and hand-outs to the Russian space programme, and Russian components do not even meet American safety standards."

### Piège à éviter
Ne réponds jamais "True" ou "False" seul : la consigne demande explicitement de justifier, et une réponse sans justification textuelle perd la totalité des points même si la case cochée est la bonne.

L'expression "a pointless castle in the sky" apparaît dans la dernière phrase du texte, en résumé de toute la démonstration : la station est un ouvrage impressionnant mais coûteux et sans réelle utilité scientifique, alors qu'une mission habitée directe vers Mars coûterait, elle, moins d'un tiers du prix de la station (environ 30 milliards de dollars contre plus de 100 milliards).
